3 Results

3.1 Accounts and reductions

Between 1990 and 2024, disaggregating natural disturbance cut the standard deviation of Canada’s annual net emissions from 190 to 24 Mt CO2e, a factor of 7.9. Fig. 1 plotted the undisaggregated and disaggregated accounts for Canada and British Columbia over the same years. The account Canada reported averaged 44.6 ± 24.0 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 36.3 to 52.8). Without the disaggregation, the same land averaged 119.9 ± 190.0 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 54.7 to 185.2). In 2023, Canada reported −8.7 Mt where the undisaggregated account showed 991 Mt. British Columbia’s reported account averaged 27.2 ± 14.9 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 22.0 to 32.3). Without the disaggregation, the province’s account averaged 60.8 ± 99.4 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 26.6 to 94.9), a standard deviation 6.7 times larger. In 2023, the province reported 19 Mt against 399 Mt. On the forest fire series, the 13 year baseline of the threshold rule classed 2015, 2018, 2021, 2023 and 2024 as natural.

On the account Canada reported, reductions were positive in 6 of the 8 years from 2017 to 2024 and summed to 85.6 Mt CO2e. Without the disaggregation, reductions were positive in only 2 years. In 2023 alone, the undisaggregated account’s net emissions rose 853.6 Mt above its five-year mean, 10 times the reductions of the account Canada reported (Table 1). The threshold account gave larger reductions than either, because its five-year mean kept the natural disturbance line in every reference year but 2015. The account then left the line out of 2018, 2021, 2023 and 2024, the later years the rule classed as natural. The threshold account’s five-year mean was 91.7 Mt, against 25.7 Mt for the account Canada reported and 137.7 Mt for the undisaggregated account. The threshold account’s reductions were positive in 5 of the 8 years and summed to 396.2 Mt, 4.6 times those of the account Canada reported (Table 1). British Columbia, with 22.2 per cent of the area burned in Canada in 2023, showed the same pattern more strongly. Online Resource 1 gave the province’s net emissions, five-year mean and reduction for each account and year. The province’s reported reductions were positive in 8 of 8 years and summed to 104.6 Mt, while its undisaggregated net emissions rose 322 Mt above their five-year mean in 2023. Under the threshold rule, the province’s net emissions rose most above their five-year mean in 2017. The national test classed 2017 as ordinary, although the province burned 1,222,365 hectares, 4.6 times its own threshold.

3.2 Treatment comparison

On Canada’s record, the positive reductions over 2017 to 2024 depended on the treatment and, for the threshold rule and the background level, on the baseline (Table 2). Canada’s approach gave positive reductions of 85.6 Mt CO2e and no disaggregation 111.7 Mt. The threshold rule gave 396.2 Mt on the forest fire series at 13 years and 396.2 Mt at 16 years. On the line, it gave 468.9, 396.2 and 468.9 Mt at 13, 20 and 27 years. On burned area, its positive reductions fell from 391.5 to 258.1 Mt once the baseline reached 27 years. The background level on the line fell as its baseline lengthened, from 62.1 Mt CO2e a year on 13 years to 0.6 on 27 years. The natural disturbance line had been a net sink in most years from 1990 to 2001, so a longer baseline held a lower mean. The positive reductions under the background level on the line therefore rose with the baseline, from 232.8 to 466.5 Mt. Every treatment except no disaggregation left emissions out of the accounts. Canada’s approach left out 2,392 Mt, and the background level on the line 1,849 to 2,157 Mt.

readr::write_csv(treatments_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-treatments.csv")
fmt_tbl(treatments_table, right = names(treatments_table)[3:9])

Burned area in the composite rose 14.8 per cent a decade from 1972 to 2024 (95 per cent confidence interval −0.4 to 32.4). The trend fell short of significance at the 5 per cent level [t(51) = 1.949, p = 0.057]. The natural disturbance line rose 55.7 Mt CO2e for each million hectares burned (95 per cent confidence interval 46.9 to 64.5) [t(32) = 12.893, p < 0.001]. The line also rose 9.9 Mt a year besides (95 per cent confidence interval 7.8 to 12.1) [t(32) = 9.294, p < 0.001], with R² = 0.92.

With management fixed, natural disturbance alone gave every treatment but Canada’s an expected net debit on a 13 year baseline, a mean annual reduction below zero (Table 2). On a 13 year baseline, the mean annual reduction differed by treatment [F(4, 7996) = 911.910, p < 0.001]. It was lowest with no disaggregation, at −79.5 ± 177.1 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −83.4 to −75.6). It was highest under Canada’s approach, zero by construction, because the approach left the whole line out. The threshold rule on burned area averaged −53.4 ± 126.8 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −56.3 to −50.5). The background level on burned area averaged −43.4 ± 88.6 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −45.5 to −41.3). On the line, the background level averaged −12.6 ± 82.0 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −14.6 to −10.7). The narrowest 90 per cent half width of an annual reduction was 108 Mt, for the background level on burned area on 45 years. On a 13 year baseline, the half width was 129 Mt for the background level on the line and 146 Mt on burned area. The threshold rule’s half width was 200 Mt, and that of no disaggregation 294 Mt.

Lengthening the baseline moved each treatment’s mean annual reduction by at most 17.2 Mt CO2e a year, against 84.1 Mt between treatments. The baseline changed the mean of the threshold rule [F(4, 7996) = 17.307, p < 0.001]. The mean of the background level also changed with the baseline, on burned area [F(4, 7996) = 10.919, p < 0.001] and on the line [F(2, 3998) = 178.953, p < 0.001]. The largest shift was that of the background level on the line, between 13 and 27 years. On 27 years, the background level on the line averaged 4.6 ± 91.5 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 2.6 to 6.6), an expected net credit. Of the three test-based runs, the background level on burned area moved least, by 3.1 Mt a year across its baselines. Within single histories, moving from the shortest to the longest baseline changed the threshold rule’s mean annual reduction by −96.6 to 70.8 Mt a year, the 5th to 95th percentiles. The same change was −64.4 to 51.5 Mt for the background level on burned area and −64.8 to 93.3 Mt on the line. Only the burned area composite allowed a baseline of 30 years or more before 2017, at 35 and 45 years.

The expected net debits came from the trends of the histories (Table 2). Without the line’s year term, no disaggregation averaged −14.9 ± 175.1 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −18.8 to −11.0) on a 13 year baseline. The three test-based treatments then expected net credits. The largest was that of the background level on burned area, at 10.6 ± 84.8 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval 8.5 to 12.8). Without either trend, no disaggregation averaged 0.0 ± 137.0 Mt CO2e a year (95 per cent confidence interval −3.2 to 3.1). The test-based treatments then averaged 7.9 to 11.7 Mt CO2e a year, all expected net credits.

3.3 Reduction uncertainty

readr::write_csv(uncertainty_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-uncertainty.csv")
fmt_tbl(uncertainty_table)

Each reduction on the account Canada reported was smaller than half its 90 per cent interval. Across the 6 years with a positive mean reduction, the half width ran from 163 to 3,692 per cent of the mean. The adjustment factor of Equation 8 ran from 51.8 to 1,176.9 per cent, and Online Resource 2 gave the draws’ mean, spread and interval for every account and year. In 2023, the mean reduction of 34.4 Mt had a standard deviation of 33.8 Mt and a 90 per cent interval of −21 to 91 Mt. On the threshold account, the adjustment factor ran from 17.9 to 28.1 per cent, because its reductions were larger, not because its emissions were more certain.

The Monte Carlo draws gave each year its own model error, independent of every other year. Model error that was the same in every year would drop out when a year was compared with the five-year mean, and the interval would narrow. With half of the error variance shared in this way, the half width on the account Canada reported ran from 115 to 2,610 per cent of the mean. The buffer was 25 per cent, and 30 per cent after 2020, when the account first rose above its mean. After the deduction and the buffer, 2 of the 6 positive years kept some of their reduction. With 90 per cent shared, the half width ran from 51 to 1,167 per cent and 4 years kept some. All 6 years kept some only when more than 99.6 per cent of the error variance was shared. Each year’s own error was then 6.4 per cent of the published standard deviation. Nothing was kept above a half width of 235 per cent with a 25 per cent buffer, 298 with 5 per cent and 220 with 30 per cent. Summed over the eight years, the reductions of the account Canada reported came to 64.8 Mt with a half width of 358 per cent. The deduction was then 114 per cent, so nothing was kept. The threshold account’s summed reductions of 161.1 Mt had a half width of 144 per cent. With a 25 per cent buffer, 29 per cent of them, 46.8 Mt, was kept.

4 Discussion

On Canada’s 2026 national greenhouse gas inventory, the treatment of the natural disturbance line decided whether net emissions and removals fell below their 2012 to 2016 mean. Canada’s inventory kept the line out of the account it reported so that the effect of human activities on the trend would be better understood (Kurz et al., 2018). Between 2017 and 2024, net emissions and removals fell below the mean in 2 of the 8 years with no disaggregation and in 6 under Canada’s approach. Every treatment added none, part or all of the line to the account Canada reported, so the differences between treatments came from the line alone (Table 2). The revised harvest record moved 34 million hectares between the two components, with “a compensating change in the natural disturbance component resulting in a small change in the total emissions” (Kurz et al., 2024, p. 1381).

Lengthening the baseline changed the reductions on the observed record (Table 2), but it changed the expected reductions far less than the choice of treatment did (Section 3.2). Fire regime studies described fire over periods longer than any of these baselines. Under random fire, the expected distribution of stand ages was the negative exponential, so that “the present age-class structure of such a forest is the key to its past fire history” (Wagner, 1978). The negative exponential and Weibull models became the standard descriptions of fire history (Johnson & Wagner, 1985). Fire cycles reported for Canada ran from 50 to 90 years in Alberta to 769 years in Newfoundland (Arsenault et al., 2016; Johnson & Larsen, 1991). Eastern Canada had a cycle of 229 years and central Quebec one of 247 years (Bélisle et al., 2011; Cyr et al., 2016). In British Columbia, the age-class distribution of a sub-boreal landscape gave a stand-replacing fire cycle of 80 to 100 years and lacked stability (Andison, 2009). In the province’s central interior, disturbance by fire and mountain pine beetle on 1 million hectares was less frequent in 1954 to 2004 than in 1904 to 1953 (Campbell, 2011). Only the burned area composite reached the 30 years of the rule of thumb for Student’s t (Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.77). The composite’s 45 years before 2017 were still shorter than the shortest of these cycles.

The estimates of a fire cycle also depended on the record behind them, as the background level on the line depended on the length of its baseline (Section 3.2). Lengthening a Landsat series in Portugal from 22 to 31 years substantially changed the fitted Weibull parameters (Oliveira et al., 2011). Parametric estimates of the fire cycle were degraded by short-term variation in fire activity (Cyr et al., 2016). The accuracy of Weibull fire intervals fell as the record of fire scars degraded (Parsons et al., 2007). A censored tail of old stands, the oldest stands cut off from the record, could falsely suggest that fire frequency had changed (Finney, 1995). A normal fire year was defined, by analogy with climate normals, from 26-year means around Yosemite (Lutz et al., 2011). Charcoal records spanning millennia were proposed as the baseline wherever recent fires were too few (Gavin et al., 2007).

The natural disturbance line rose over the record (Section 3.2), so a longer baseline gave a lower background level. The line was a net sink in 10 of the 12 years from 1990 to 2001 and a net source in every year from 2002. The early sink came from the regrowth of stands burned before 1990, which Canada’s inventory kept on the line until they were old enough to harvest (Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.74). The 2013 Kyoto Protocol Supplement built its background level from the annual emissions of natural disturbances, whereas the line also included the removals of their regrowth (IPCC, 2014, p. 2.46). The Supplement encouraged “the longest available time series”, and its default method removed only high years, because removing low ones “would lead to the expectation of net credits” (IPCC, 2014, pp. 2.46, 2.49). On Canada’s record, lengthening the baseline as the Supplement encouraged took in more of the trend that its first condition required to be absent. Without the trend, the three test-based treatments expected net credits instead (Section 3.2), the outcome the Supplement’s conditions were set to avoid (IPCC, 2014, p. 2.50).

On burned area, leaving out only the excess above a background level did better on both measures than leaving out whole years (Table 2). In a natural year, Australia’s inventory moved all wildfire emissions of each state that passed its test out of the human-induced total (Bowman et al., 2023, p. 4). With a 13 year baseline, the background level gave a smaller expected net debit and a narrower half width on the natural disturbance line than on burned area. The test series therefore moved both measures more than the choice between excluding the excess and excluding the whole year. On the observed record, the threshold rule gave the larger positive reductions, 391.5 Mt against 111.7 Mt on 13 years, despite its larger expected net debit and half width.

Canada’s approach was the only treatment with neither an expected net debit nor an expected net credit, because it left the whole line out of every year. Between 2017 and 2024, the approach left out 2,392 Mt CO2e of the line (Table 2). The line included every wildfire in the managed forest whatever its ignition (ECCC, 2026), and 92 per cent of the area burned in Canada in 2023 had a natural cause (Canadian Forest Service, 2026a). Canada’s approach depended on the 2019 Refinement’s expectation that the carbon dioxide of natural disturbances would be “balanced by subsequent removals” with “no established time limit” (Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.69). The Refinement expected natural effects to average out only “provided that there are no trends in disturbance rates, such as increased annual area burned as a result of climate change” (Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.68). On Canada’s record, the line rose and was a net source in every year from 2002, although the rise in burned area fell short of significance (Section 3.2). The methane and nitrous oxide of wildfires on the line could not balance, because “non-CO2 emissions are not taken up by vegetation” (ECCC, 2026, p. 203; Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.72). Canada’s inventory returned a stand to the anthropogenic component at the end of a recovery period of 60 to 100 years, as the Refinement allowed (Kurz et al., 2024, p. 1377; Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.72). Between 2005 and 2021, harvest, regrowth after harvest and wood products were a net source of 90.8 Mt CO2e a year, against a reported net sink of 4.7 Mt (Bysouth et al., 2024). Bysouth et al. (2024) explained the difference by the removals of stands of natural disturbance origin after their return to the anthropogenic component.

The disaggregation cut the standard deviation of annual net emissions (Section 3.1) but did not make the reductions of the account Canada reported precise (Section 3.3). Canada’s inventory gave the carbon dioxide of forest land remaining forest land in 2024 as −1.9 Mt, with 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of −63 and 19 Mt (ECCC, 2026, p. 206). Under Equations 8 and 27 of ART TREES, the adjustment factor exceeded 100 per cent in 4 of the 6 positive years, so the deduction was larger than the reduction (ART, 2026b, pp. 58, 69). The interval on the reductions came from the published uncertainty of CBM-CFS3 alone, so it included only model error (Metsaranta et al., 2017). The draws also treated each year’s error as independent, and varying the common share bounded that assumption without removing it. Every positive year kept part of its reduction only when more than 99.6 per cent of the error variance was common to all years.

The 2019 Refinement left four choices to each country (Ogle et al., 2019, pp. 2.67–2.78). The first was the record behind the test, which the European Union set at 2001 to 2020 for its background level (European Union, 2018). Verra’s risk tool for land use projects counted natural events over the last 100 years and extrapolated from records of 20 years or more (Verra, 2024, p. 17). The European Union’s earlier reference levels, projected rather than drawn from a record, had counted removals “mostly” from “policy-assumed harvest increases that never materialized” (Grassi et al., 2018). The second was the regrowth period, which was 60 to 100 years in Canada, typically 11 years in Australia and 20 years in the European example (Kurz et al., 2024; Ogle et al., 2019, pp. 2.73, 2.77). The third was the form of the exclusion, the excess above a background level or the whole year (IPCC, 2014, p. 2.50). The fourth was whether the split was made by stand or by landscape, which affected “the annual disaggregation” while “in the long term the totals are the same” (Ogle et al., 2019, p. 2.72). A reduction against a five year mean depended on the annual split, not on the long-term total.

Where removals equalled emissions, the uncertainty chapter noted that “the denominator in the Equation 3.2 is equal to ‘0’ and the formula has no sense” (Paciornik et al., 2019, p. 3.19). The numerator of Equation 3.2, the combined uncertainty in tonnes, stayed finite, as did a percentage of gross emissions or of gross removals. The Forest Carbon Partnership Facility set its deduction for uncertainty in steps, from none at 15 per cent or less to 15 per cent above 100 per cent (Forest Carbon Partnership Facility, 2024, p. 7). The 2024 IPCC expert meeting raised concerns that a disaggregated estimate would be “difficult to impossible” for countries to verify with observations (IPCC, 2024, p. 16). A review for the United States concluded that “disturbance risks must be accounted for in carbon offset protocols, carbon management practices, and carbon mapping and modeling techniques” (Dye et al., 2024). Every treatment used the inventory’s figures as reported, so the comparison tested the treatments rather than the model behind the line.

5 Conclusions

The treatment of natural disturbance changed Canada’s expected reductions more than the baseline length did. In the simulated histories, the choice between treatments moved the mean annual reduction from natural disturbance alone 5 times as far as any change of baseline. Among the three test-based treatments alone, the ratio was 2.4. On a 13 year baseline, every treatment that counted any of the natural disturbance line had an expected net debit, which came from the line’s trend. Without that trend, the test-based treatments expected net credits instead. Canada’s approach, which counted none of the line, depended on a balance between emissions and later removals that had no set time limit. On a 13 year baseline, the background level on the line had the smallest expected net debit and the narrowest range of the treatments that counted the line. Even so, a one-year change in management smaller than about 129 Mt CO2e could not be told apart from natural disturbance at the 90 per cent level. The records set the limit on baseline length, since only the burned area composite reached the 30 years of the rule of thumb for Student’s t. A percentage uncertainty on a reduction near zero was not informative, while the same interval in tonnes remained finite.

```{r}
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL) {
  df <- dplyr::mutate(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of("Year"), as.integer))
  right <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  flextable::flextable(df) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::align(j = setdiff(names(df), right), align = "left", part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(j = right, align = "right", part = "body") |>
    flextable::colformat_int(big.mark = "") |>
    flextable::padding(padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1, part = "all") |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}
```

```{r}
# FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (domain GI), FAO, Rome
# https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GI
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv") &&
    nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD"))) {
  login <- httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/auth/login") |>
    httr2::req_body_form(username = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER"),
                         password = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD")) |>
    httr2::req_perform() |>
    httr2::resp_body_json()
  httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/en/data/GI") |>
    httr2::req_url_query(area = "33", area_cs = "FAO", output_type = "csv") |>
    httr2::req_auth_bearer_token(login$AuthenticationResult$AccessToken) |>
    httr2::req_perform(path = "02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv")
}

fires <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(item = Item, element = Element, year = Year, source = Source,
                value = Value, unit = Unit, flag = Flag)

forest_co2 <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", element == "Emissions (CO2)", source == "FAO TIER 1") |>
  dplyr::select(year, co2 = value)

forest <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", source == "FAO TIER 1",
                element %in% c("Burned Area", "Emissions (CO2)", "Emissions (CH4)"), year >= 2001) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename(Year = year, `Burned area (ha)` = `Burned Area`,
                `CO2 (kt)` = `Emissions (CO2)`, `CH4 (kt)` = `Emissions (CH4)`)

gap <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Other forest", element == "Emissions (CO2)") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = source, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(`FAO TIER 1`), !is.na(UNFCCC)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year, `FAO Tier 1 (kt)` = `FAO TIER 1`, `UNFCCC (kt)` = UNFCCC,
                   Ratio = round(`FAO TIER 1` / UNFCCC, 1))

# Tables 2.4 and 2.5 of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Volume 4, Chapter 2, pages 2.45 to 2.47, the tables the FAOSTAT methodological note cites
# http://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/index.html
table_2_4 <- tibble::tribble(~fuel, ~se, ~`IPCC biomass consumption row`,
  41.0, 36.5, "All boreal forest", 50.4, 53.7, "All other temperate forests", 3.3, NA, "Savanna woodland, mid or late dry season burns",
  4.1, 3.1, "Grassland, mid or late dry season burns", 14.3, 9.0, "All shrublands", 26.7, 4.2, "Shrubland (general)")
table_2_5 <- tibble::tribble(~ef_row, ~co2, ~co2_sd, ~ch4, ~ch4_sd, ~n2o, ~n2o_sd,
  "Savanna and grassland", 1613, 95, 2.3, 0.9, 0.21, 0.10, "Extra tropical forest", 1569, 131, 4.7, 1.9, 0.26, 0.07)
used <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% c("Other forest", "Woody savanna", "Savanna", "Grassland", "Open shrubland", "Closed shrubland")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2", "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o", .default = "dm")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(item, year), names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(ha > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dm / ha, dplyr::across(c(co2, ch4, n2o), \(x) x * 1e6 / dm))
coefficients <- used |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = item, years = dplyr::n(), ha = sum(ha) / 24, fuel_min = min(fuel), fuel_max = max(fuel),
                   co2 = mean(co2), ch4 = mean(ch4), n2o = mean(n2o)) |>
  dplyr::filter(years == 24) |>
  dplyr::arrange(item != "Other forest", -ha) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Item = item,
    `Burned area (ha a year)` = format(round(ha), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
    `Fuel (t/ha)` = dplyr::if_else(round(fuel_min, 1) == round(fuel_max, 1), sprintf("%.1f", fuel_min), sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", fuel_min, fuel_max)),
    `IPCC biomass consumption row` = dplyr::coalesce(table_2_4$`IPCC biomass consumption row`[match(round(fuel_min, 1), table_2_4$fuel)], "Between all boreal forest and all other temperate forests"),
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", ch4), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", n2o),
    `CO2 (g/kg)` = dplyr::if_else(is.na(co2), "", format(round(co2), big.mark = ","))) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(Item = "Emission factor row, extra tropical forest", `Burned area (ha a year)` = "", `Fuel (t/ha)` = "", `IPCC biomass consumption row` = "",
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", table_2_5$ch4[2]), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", table_2_5$n2o[2]), `CO2 (g/kg)` = format(table_2_5$co2[2], big.mark = ",")))
savanna_share <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, element == "Burned Area", item %in% c("Forest fires", "Savanna fires")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = item, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = 100 * `Savanna fires` / (`Savanna fires` + `Forest fires`))

# FAO AllFires_OrganicSoils, related document of FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (GI)
# https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GI
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv")) {
  flat <- gsub("[\n ]+", " ",
    paste(pdftools::pdf_text("02.inputs/faostat/raw/AllFires_OrganicSoils.pdf"), collapse = "\n"))
  rx <- paste0("[0-9]+,(?:\"[^\"]*\"|[^,]*),6993,Fires in organic soils,",
               "(?:CH4 emissions|CO2 emissions|Burned Area|Biomass burned [(]dry matter[)]),",
               "[0-9]{4},[0-9.eE+-]+,(?:ha|tonnes|kilotonnes)")
  readr::write_lines(
    c("area_code,area,item_code,item,element,year,value,unit",
      regmatches(flat, gregexpr(rx, flat))[[1]]),
    "02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv")
}

peat <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(peat) == dplyr::n_distinct(peat$area) * dplyr::n_distinct(peat$year) * 4)

canada <- peat |>
  dplyr::filter(area == "Canada", element %in% c("Burned Area", "CO2 emissions", "CH4 emissions")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>

                `CO2 (kt)` = `CO2 emissions`, `CH4 (kt)` = `CH4 emissions`)

obs  <- canada[canada$Year >= 2001, ]
post <- canada[canada$Year >= 1996, ]
fill <- canada[["Burned area (ha)"]][1]

# Table 6-1, Net Greenhouse Gas Flux Estimates in the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry Sector,
# All Inventory Years, by province and territory, Environment and Climate Change Canada,
# National Inventory Report 1990-2024
# https://data-donnees.az.ec.gc.ca/data/substances/monitor/canada-s-official-greenhouse-gas-inventory/E-LULUCF/?lang=en
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/eccc/lulucf-2026.csv")) {
  dir.create("02.inputs/eccc/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  download.file(paste0("https://data-donnees.az.ec.gc.ca/api/file?path=", URLencode("/substances/monitor/canada-s-official-greenhouse-gas-inventory/E-LULUCF/NIR2026_Table 6-1_All_Years_PTs.xlsx", reserved = TRUE)), "02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx", mode = "wb")
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets("02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx")
  c(Canada = "NATIONAL$", BC = " BC$") |>
    purrr::map(\(s) readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx", sheet = grep(s, sheets, value = TRUE), skip = 3, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "unique_quiet")) |>
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "region") |>
    dplyr::mutate(component = dplyr::case_when(grepl("TOTAL", ...1) ~ "human", grepl("^Natural disturbances", ...2) ~ "natural")) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(component)) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::matches("^[0-9]{4}$"), names_to = "year", values_to = "kt") |>
    dplyr::transmute(region, component, year = as.integer(year), mt = as.numeric(kt) / 1000) |>

eccc <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/eccc/lulucf-2026.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(net = human + natural)
stopifnot(nrow(eccc) == 2 * 35, !anyNA(eccc))

national <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "Canada")

# Canadian National Fire Database, fire polygons, Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Forest Service
# https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/ha/nfdb
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/nfdb/area-burned-by-province.csv")) {
  dir.create("02.inputs/nfdb", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  Sys.setenv(GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN = "EMPTY_DIR", CPL_VSIL_CURL_USE_HEAD = "NO")
  zip <- paste0("/vsizip//vsicurl/https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nfdb/",
                "fire_poly/current_version/NFDB_poly.zip")
  lapply(c("NFDB_poly_1972to2020_20250630", "NFDB_poly_2021to2024_20250630"), function(layer)
    sf::st_drop_geometry(sf::st_read(zip, quiet = TRUE,
      query = sprintf('SELECT SRC_AGENCY, YEAR, SIZE_HA FROM "%s"', layer)))) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |>
    dplyr::filter(YEAR >= 1990, !is.na(SIZE_HA)) |>
    dplyr::rename(province = SRC_AGENCY, year = YEAR) |>
    dplyr::summarise(hectares = sum(SIZE_HA), .by = c(province, year)) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/nfdb/area-burned-by-province.csv")

burned <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/nfdb/area-burned-by-province.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

share <- burned |>
  dplyr::summarise(bc = sum(hectares[province == "BC"]), canada = sum(hectares), .by = year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = bc / canada)

bc <- eccc |>
  dplyr::filter(region == "BC") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(share, year, share), by = "year")

trees_uncertainty <- function(ci_half_width) 0.524417 / 1.645006 * ci_half_width

buffer_table <- c(none = 0.25, `1` = 0.20, `2` = 0.15, `3` = 0.20,
                  `1,2` = 0.10, `1,3` = 0.15, `2,3` = 0.10, `1,2,3` = 0.05)

trees_buffer <- function(mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  buffer_table[[mitigating]] + if (after_reversal) 0.05 else 0
}

kept <- function(ci_half_width, mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  1 - trees_uncertainty(ci_half_width) - trees_buffer(mitigating, after_reversal)
}

break_even <- function(...) (1 - trees_buffer(...)) / (0.524417 / 1.645006)

crediting_level <- function(x, years) sum(x[years]) / 5

accounts <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016)

level_split  <- sum(accounts$human[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_whole  <- sum(accounts$net[accounts$reference]) / 5

credits <- accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(!reference) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year,
                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = human,
                   `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_split - human, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = net,
                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_whole - net, 1))

split_pos <- credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
whole_pos <- credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
worst <- which.min(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

bc_accounts <- bc |> dplyr::filter(year >= 2012)
bc_level_split <- sum(bc_accounts$human[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5
bc_level_whole <- sum(bc_accounts$net[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5

bc_credits <- bc_accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2017) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year,
                   `Burned area share (%)` = round(100 * share, 1),
                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(human, 1),
                   `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_split - human, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(net, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_whole - net, 1))

bc_split_pos <- bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_whole_pos <- bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

# The threshold rule on Canada's two lines: the natural disturbance line is left out only in a year whose
# forest fire emissions exceed by two standard deviations the mean of the 13 years ending in 2016, the last
# reference year, 13 years being the baseline length Australia's inventory uses
years13 <- 2004:2016
base13 <- forest_co2$co2[forest_co2$year %in% years13]
natural_years <- forest_co2$year[forest_co2$co2 > mean(base13) + 2 * stats::sd(base13)]
accounts <- dplyr::mutate(accounts, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% natural_years, human, net))
level_rule <- sum(accounts$rule[accounts$reference]) / 5
credits <- credits |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = accounts$rule[!accounts$reference],
                `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(level_rule - `Threshold rule emissions (Mt)`, 1))
rule_pos <- credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
rule_out <- credits$Year %in% natural_years
rule_worst <- which.min(credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]])

# The threshold rule's second step for British Columbia: a nationally natural year counts as natural in the province only
# when the province's burned area exceeds its own mean over the same 13 years by one standard deviation

bc_natural_years <- intersect(natural_years, bc_burned$year[bc_burned$hectares > mean(bc_base) + stats::sd(bc_base)])
bc_accounts <- dplyr::mutate(bc_accounts, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% bc_natural_years, human, net))
bc_level_rule <- sum(bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5
bc_credits <- bc_credits |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = round(bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year >= 2017], 1),
                `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_rule - bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$year >= 2017], 1))
bc_rule_pos <- bc_credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_rule_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]])
bc_threshold_ha <- mean(bc_base) + stats::sd(bc_base)

ci <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.50, 2.00)
deductions <- data.frame(
  `Uncertainty, 90% interval half width (%)` = ci * 100,
  `Uncertainty deduction (%)` = round(100 * trees_uncertainty(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 25% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 5% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, "1,2,3"), 1),
  `Kept, 30% buffer after a reversal (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, after_reversal = TRUE), 1),
  check.names = FALSE)

set.seed(42)
sd_mt <- 16.6 * (44 / 12) / 1.96

simulate_reductions <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) +
                             stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  level - (emissions + stats::rnorm(n, 0, sd_mt))
}

monte_carlo <- function(reference, series) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(series)), function(k) {
    draws <- simulate_reductions(reference, series$emissions[k])
    half <- (stats::quantile(draws, 0.95) - stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)) / 2
    data.frame(Year = series$year[k], mean = mean(draws), sd = stats::sd(draws), q05 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)),
               q95 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.95)), half = half, ci = half / abs(mean(draws)))
  }))
}

                   `5th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q05), `95th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q95),
                   `Relative half width (%)` = ifelse(mean > 0, sprintf("%.0f", 100 * ci), ""),

                    mean(x), stats::sd(x), stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[1], stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[2])
province <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "BC")

# Share of the annual error common to the reference years and the crediting year. A shared error cancels in
# the difference, the ground on which ART TREES excludes model error. The draws above share none. Under the
# normal model a shared share rho leaves the mean reduction and scales its half width by sqrt(1 - rho).
after <- credits$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos])
shared <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99), function(rho) {
  ci <- mc_split$ci * sqrt(1 - rho)
  data.frame(`Shared share` = rho,
             `Interval, lowest (%)` = round(100 * min(ci[split_pos])),
             `Interval, highest (%)` = round(100 * max(ci[split_pos])),
             `Years keeping a credit` = sum(purrr::map2_dbl(ci, after, \(h, a) kept(h, after_reversal = a))[split_pos] > 0),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
sh <- function(share, column) shared[[column]][shared[["Shared share"]] == share]
# The shared share at which every positive year keeps a credit, solved from the same scaling
rho_needed <- max(1 - (purrr::map_dbl(after[split_pos], \(a) break_even(after_reversal = a)) / mc_split$ci[split_pos])^2)

# Deduction the standard allows at the end of a crediting period, on the summed reference emissions minus the
# summed crediting period emissions, with the same independent draws
simulate_period <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  total <- length(emissions) * level -
    rowSums(matrix(rep(emissions, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(emissions), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  half <- unname((stats::quantile(total, 0.95) - stats::quantile(total, 0.05)) / 2)
  centre <- length(emissions) * mean(reference) - sum(emissions)
  c(total = centre, half = half, ci = half / abs(centre))
}
period_split <- simulate_period(reference_split, credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]])
period_rule <- simulate_period(accounts$rule[accounts$reference], credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]])
period_deduction <- period_split[["total"]] * trees_uncertainty(period_split[["ci"]])

u_fuel <- u_term(table_2_4$se[1:2], table_2_4$fuel[1:2])
u_ef <- u_term(table_2_5$co2_sd[1], table_2_5$co2[1])

  ((table_2_5$ch4[2] - table_2_5$ch4[1]) * 28 + (table_2_5$n2o[2] - table_2_5$n2o[1]) * 265) / 1e9
```

```{r}
#| label: treatments

# National Burned Area Composite (NBAC), summary statistics by year and administrative unit, 1972 to 2025, Canadian Forest Service
# https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/ and the file https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx")) {
  dir.create("02.inputs/nrcan/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  download.file("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", mode = "wb")
}
nbac_years <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", sheet = "sumstats_admin_name", skip = 2) |>
  dplyr::transmute(year = as.integer(YEAR), ha = as.numeric(CANADA)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(year), year <= 2024)

# Default method of the 2013 Kyoto Protocol Supplement, p. 2.49: years above the mean plus twice the standard deviation are removed
# until none remains, and the final mean and twice the final standard deviation are the background level and the margin
background_level <- function(x) {
  repeat {
    outlier <- x > mean(x) + 2 * stats::sd(x)
    if (!any(outlier)) return(c(level = mean(x), margin = 2 * stats::sd(x)))
    x <- x[!outlier]
  }
}

# A baseline of n years ends in 2016, the last reference year, and each account is compared with its own 2012 to 2016 mean
in_window <- function(years, n) years >= 2017 - n & years <= 2016
reduce <- function(account, years) round(mean(account[years %in% 2012:2016]) - account, 1)[years %in% 2017:2024]
num <- \(x, d = 1) gsub("-(?=[0-9])", "\u2212", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), round(x, d) + 0), perl = TRUE)

# The four treatments of the natural disturbance line nd: none, Canada's, the threshold rule on a test series, and the Kyoto
# background level, applied to the line itself or, through the share of burned area above the background, to a burned area series
treat <- function(human, nd, years, test, test_years, n, method) {
  now <- test[match(years, test_years)]
  base <- test[in_window(test_years, n)]
  counted <- switch(method,
    none = nd,
    canada = 0 * nd,
    threshold = ifelse(now > mean(base) + 2 * stats::sd(base), 0, nd),
    kyoto_line = { b <- background_level(nd[in_window(years, n)]); ifelse(nd > b[["level"]] + b[["margin"]], b[["level"]], nd) },
    kyoto_area = { b <- background_level(base); ifelse(now > b[["level"]] + b[["margin"]], nd * b[["level"]] / now, nd) })
  list(reductions = reduce(human + counted, years), excluded = sum((nd - counted)[years %in% 2017:2024]))
}

tests <- list(none = list(national$natural, national$year), canada = list(national$natural, national$year),
              `FAOSTAT forest fire CO2` = list(forest_co2$co2, forest_co2$year),
              `Natural disturbance line` = list(national$natural, national$year), `NBAC burned area` = list(nbac_years$ha, nbac_years$year))
runs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(method = c("none", "canada"), series = c("none", "canada"), n = 13),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "FAOSTAT forest fire CO2", n = c(13, 16)),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "Natural disturbance line", n = c(13, 20, 27)),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "NBAC burned area", n = c(13, 20, 27, 35, 45)),
  tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_line", series = "Natural disturbance line", n = c(13, 20, 27)),
  tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_area", series = "NBAC burned area", n = c(13, 20, 27, 35, 45)))
treatments_observed <- purrr::pmap(runs, function(method, series, n) {
  out <- treat(national$human, national$natural, national$year, tests[[series]][[1]], tests[[series]][[2]], n, method)
  tibble::tibble(method, series, n, positive = sum(out$reductions[out$reductions > 0]), years_positive = sum(out$reductions > 0),
                 net = sum(out$reductions), excluded = out$excluded)
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
readr::write_csv(treatments_observed, "03.outputs/TBL/treatments-observed.csv")

# Simulated fire histories with management fixed: burned area follows the NBAC log-linear trend with resampled residuals, the
# natural disturbance line follows its regression on burned area and year with resampled residuals, and the rest of the land use
# sector stays at its 2012 to 2016 mean, so every reduction comes from natural disturbance and from the treatment
set.seed(2026)
fit_area <- stats::lm(log(ha) ~ year, nbac_years)
fit_line <- stats::lm(natural ~ I(ha / 1e6) + year, dplyr::inner_join(national, nbac_years, by = "year"))
human_flat <- rep(mean(national$human[national$year %in% 2012:2016]), nrow(national))
sim_runs <- dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(method = c("none", "canada"), n = 13), tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", n = c(13, 20, 27, 35, 45)),
                             tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_line", n = c(13, 20, 27)), tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_area", n = c(13, 20, 27, 35, 45)))
# The composite's table runs from 2024 back to 1972, so each simulated year's burned area is matched to the line's year
# by match(), not by position. year_term = FALSE holds the line's year term at 2014, the middle of the reference period,
# and area_trend = FALSE holds burned area at the mean of its fitted log values, so the two checks remove each trend in turn
simulate_histories <- function(year_term = TRUE, area_trend = TRUE, histories = 2000, seed = 2026) {
  set.seed(seed)
  area_fit <- if (area_trend) stats::fitted(fit_area) else rep(mean(stats::fitted(fit_area)), nrow(nbac_years))
  line_year <- if (year_term) national$year else rep(2014, nrow(national))
  replicate(histories, {
    ha <- exp(area_fit + sample(stats::residuals(fit_area), replace = TRUE))
    nd <- stats::predict(fit_line, data.frame(ha = ha[match(national$year, nbac_years$year)], year = line_year)) +
      sample(stats::residuals(fit_line), replace = TRUE)
    unlist(purrr::pmap(sim_runs, function(method, n) treat(human_flat, nd, national$year, ha, nbac_years$year, n, method)$reductions))
  })
}
draws <- simulate_histories()
# The eight crediting years of one history share its reference mean and its baseline, so the 95 per cent interval of
# each mean and the tests below rest on the history means, one per history, rather than on every year of every history
hist_means <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(sim_runs)), function(i) colMeans(draws[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, , drop = FALSE]), numeric(ncol(draws))))
ci95 <- function(x) if (stats::sd(x) > 0) stats::t.test(x)$conf.int else c(mean(x), mean(x))
treatments_simulated <- purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(sim_runs)), function(i) {
  x <- as.vector(draws[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, ])
  tibble::tibble(sim_runs[i, ], bias = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), ci_low = ci95(hist_means[i, ])[1], ci_high = ci95(hist_means[i, ])[2],
                 half_width = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.95) - stats::quantile(x, 0.05)) / 2)
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
readr::write_csv(treatments_simulated, "03.outputs/TBL/treatments-simulated.csv")

# The two trend checks, summarised like the main run: the line's year term held at 2014, then burned area also held
# at the mean of its fitted log values
summarise_runs <- function(d) purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(sim_runs)), function(i) {
  x <- as.vector(d[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, ]); ci <- ci95(colMeans(d[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, , drop = FALSE]))
  tibble::tibble(sim_runs[i, ], bias = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), ci_low = ci[1], ci_high = ci[2])
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
treatments_sensitivity <- dplyr::bind_rows(full = summarise_runs(draws),
                                           no_year_term = summarise_runs(simulate_histories(year_term = FALSE)),
                                           no_trend = summarise_runs(simulate_histories(year_term = FALSE, area_trend = FALSE)), .id = "check")
readr::write_csv(treatments_sensitivity, "03.outputs/TBL/treatments-sensitivity.csv")

# Repeated-measures analysis of variance on the history means, with the history as the subject, across the five runs
# on a 13 year baseline and across the baselines of each treatment that ran on more than one
rm_anova <- function(rows) {
  y <- hist_means[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  k <- nrow(y); h <- ncol(y); g <- mean(y)
  ss_t <- h * sum((rowMeans(y) - g)^2)
  ss_e <- sum((y - g)^2) - ss_t - k * sum((colMeans(y) - g)^2)
  f <- (ss_t / (k - 1)) / (ss_e / ((k - 1) * (h - 1)))
  tibble::tibble(df1 = k - 1, df2 = (k - 1) * (h - 1), F = f, p = stats::pf(f, k - 1, (k - 1) * (h - 1), lower.tail = FALSE))
}
treatment_tests <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(test = "treatments", rm_anova(which(sim_runs$n == 13))),
  purrr::map(c("threshold", "kyoto_line", "kyoto_area"), \(m) tibble::tibble(test = m, rm_anova(which(sim_runs$method == m)))) |> purrr::list_rbind())
readr::write_csv(treatment_tests, "03.outputs/TBL/treatments-tests.csv")
fmt_f <- function(t) with(dplyr::filter(treatment_tests, test == t),

         ", p ", if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)), "]"))
# The t statistic of one regression coefficient, in the form the Results print
fmt_t <- function(fit, term) {
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients[term, ]
  paste0("[t(", stats::df.residual(fit), ") = ", formatC(s[[3]], format = "f", digits = 3), ", p ",
         if (s[[4]] < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", formatC(s[[4]], format = "f", digits = 3)), "]")
}
baseline_shift <- sapply(split(treatments_simulated$bias, treatments_simulated$method), function(x) diff(range(x)))

treatment_names <- c(none = "No disaggregation", canada = "Canada's approach", threshold = "Threshold rule", kyoto_line = "Background level", kyoto_area = "Background level")
treatment_series <- c(none = "", canada = "", threshold = "NBAC burned area", kyoto_line = "Natural disturbance line", kyoto_area = "NBAC burned area")

tr <- \(m, n, s = NULL) dplyr::filter(treatments_observed, method == m, n == !!n, if (is.null(s)) TRUE else series == s)
tsim <- \(m, n) dplyr::filter(treatments_simulated, method == m, n == !!n)
sim_msd <- \(m, n) with(tsim(m, n), paste0(num(bias), " ± ", num(sd), " Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval ", num(ci_low), " to ", num(ci_high), ")"))
```

```{r}
#| label: zones

# FAO Global Ecological Zones, second edition (GEZ 2010), the ecological zones of Table 4.1 of Volume 4, Chapter 4 of the 2006 Guidelines
# https://data.apps.fao.org/catalog/dataset/2fb209d0-fd34-4e5e-a3d8-a13c241eb61b
# IPCC default soil classes, the 5 arc-minute raster derived from the Harmonized World Soil Database version 1.1 by Batjes (2010), ISRIC Report 2009/02b,
# legend from its Idrisi sidecar SOIL_TYPE.RDC; 02.inputs/README.md records no retrieval link, so the Canada crop is committed as 02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif
# MODIS/Terra+Aqua Land Cover Type Yearly L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, MCD12Q1 version 6.1, band LC_Type1 (IGBP classes), year 2023, read through Google Earth Engine at 2 km
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD12Q1.061
# Canadian National Fire Database, fire points, Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Forest Service
# https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/ha/nfdb
dir.create("02.inputs/ipcc/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("02.inputs/nfdb/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez2010.zip"))
  download.file("https://storage.googleapis.com/fao-maps-catalog-data/uuid/2fb209d0-fd34-4e5e-a3d8-a13c241eb61b/resources/gez2010.zip",
                "02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez2010.zip", mode = "wb")
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip"))
  download.file("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nfdb/fire_pnt/current_version/NFDB_point_shp.zip",
                "02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip", mode = "wb")
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif"))
  terra::crop(terra::rast("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/soil_type.tif"), terra::ext(-141.5, -52, 41, 84)) |>
    terra::writeRaster("02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif", datatype = "INT1U", gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/mcd12q1-2023-canada.tif")) {
  ee <- reticulate::import("ee")
  ee$Initialize(project = "manuscripts-personal")
  image <- ee$ImageCollection("MODIS/061/MCD12Q1")$select("LC_Type1")$filterDate("2023-01-01", "2023-12-31")$first()
  url <- image$getDownloadURL(list(scale = 2000L, crs = "EPSG:4326", format = "GEO_TIFF",
                                   region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(list(-141.5, 41, -52, 84), "EPSG:4326", FALSE)))
  download.file(url, "02.inputs/ipcc/mcd12q1-2023-canada.tif", mode = "wb")
}

sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
canada_outline <- sf::st_make_valid(rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = 50, country = "Canada", returnclass = "sf")["name"])
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg")) {
  sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez2010.zip"), "/gez_2010_wgs84.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_intersection(canada_outline) |>
    sf::st_transform(3978) |>
    sf::st_write("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
}
gez <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(gez_abbrev != "Water")
gez$mha <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(gez)) / 1e10
provinces <- rnaturalearth::ne_states(country = "Canada", returnclass = "sf")
bc <- sf::st_transform(provinces[provinces$name == "British Columbia", "name"], 3978)

soil <- terra::rast("02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif")
soil_labels <- c("Organic", "Sandy", "Wetland", "Volcanic", "Spodic", "High activity clay", "Low activity clay", "Other")
land_cover <- terra::rast("02.inputs/ipcc/mcd12q1-2023-canada.tif")
cover_labels <- c("Forest, IGBP 1 to 5", "Shrubland, IGBP 6 to 7", "Woody savanna, IGBP 8", "Savanna, IGBP 9", "Grassland, IGBP 10", "Wetland, IGBP 11", "Other")
cover_of <- function(code) dplyr::case_when(code %in% 1:5 ~ cover_labels[1], code %in% 6:7 ~ cover_labels[2], code == 8 ~ cover_labels[3],
                                            code == 9 ~ cover_labels[4], code == 10 ~ cover_labels[5], code == 11 ~ cover_labels[6], .default = cover_labels[7])

# Every fire of 2001 to 2024 placed in its ecological zone, soil class, land cover class and province, with its cause, fire type and month
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/fires-by-stratum.csv") || !file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/large-fires.gpkg")) {
  points <- sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip"), "/NFDB_point_20260811.shp"),
                        query = 'SELECT YEAR, MONTH, SIZE_HA, CAUSE, FIRE_TYPE, PRESCRIBED FROM "NFDB_point_20260811" WHERE YEAR >= 2001 AND YEAR <= 2024',
                        quiet = TRUE) |>
    sf::st_transform(3978) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cause = dplyr::case_when(CAUSE == "N" ~ "Natural", CAUSE == "H" ~ "Human", .default = "Unknown"),
                  type = dplyr::case_when(FIRE_TYPE == "Crown" ~ "Crown", FIRE_TYPE == "Surface" ~ "Surface", FIRE_TYPE == "Ground" ~ "Ground",
                                          FIRE_TYPE %in% c("Prescribed Burn", "PB") | PRESCRIBED == "PB" ~ "Prescribed", .default = "Unspecified"),
                  season = dplyr::case_when(MONTH %in% 4:5 ~ "April to May", MONTH == 6 ~ "June", MONTH == 7 ~ "July",
                                            MONTH %in% 8:10 ~ "August to October", .default = "Other months")) |>
    sf::st_join(gez[, "gez_abbrev"], join = sf::st_intersects, left = FALSE)
  wgs <- terra::vect(sf::st_transform(points, 4326))
  points$soil <- c("Unclassified", soil_labels)[dplyr::coalesce(terra::extract(soil, wgs)[, 2], 0) + 1]
  points$cover <- cover_of(terra::extract(land_cover, wgs)[, 2])
  points$bc <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(points, bc)) > 0
  sf::st_write(points[points$SIZE_HA >= 1000, c("YEAR", "SIZE_HA", "cause")], "02.inputs/ipcc/raw/large-fires.gpkg", quiet = TRUE, delete_dsn = TRUE)
  points |>
    sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
    dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(SIZE_HA), fires = dplyr::n(), .by = c(YEAR, gez_abbrev, soil, cover, cause, type, season, bc)) |>
    dplyr::rename(year = YEAR) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/ipcc/fires-by-stratum.csv")
}

pm <- function(x, s, digits) dplyr::case_when(is.na(x) ~ "", is.na(s) ~ formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits),
                                              .default = paste0(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits), " ± ", formatC(s, format = "f", digits = digits)))

  "Boreal forest", "Land clearing fire", 87.5, 35.0, 0.59, NA, "Extra tropical forest",
  "Boreal forest", "All boreal forest", 41.0, 36.5, 0.34, 0.17, "Extra tropical forest",
  "Other temperate forests", "Wildfire", 19.8, 6.3, NA, NA, "Extra tropical forest",
  "Other temperate forests", "Post logging slash burn", 77.5, 65.0, 0.62, 0.12, "Extra tropical forest",

  "Shrublands", "Shrubland (general)", 26.7, 4.2, 0.95, NA, "Savanna and grassland",
  "Shrublands", "All shrublands", 14.3, 9.0, 0.72, 0.25, "Savanna and grassland",
  "Savanna grasslands and pastures", "All savanna grasslands (early dry season burns)", 2.1, NA, 0.74, NA, "Savanna and grassland",
  "Savanna grasslands and pastures", "Grassland (mid or late dry season burns)", 4.1, 3.1, 0.77, 0.26, "Savanna and grassland",
  "Other vegetation types", "Peatland", 41, 1.4, NA, NA, NA,
  "Other vegetation types", "Tundra", 10, NA, NA, NA, "Savanna and grassland") |>
  dplyr::mutate(row = paste(vegetation, subcategory, sep = ", "))
# Table 2.6 (fuel consumption, mean and 95 per cent confidence interval) and Table 2.7 (emission factors, mean and 95 per cent interval) of
# Chapter 2 of the 2013 Wetlands Supplement, pages 2.40 and 2.41, boreal and temperate rows, carbon dioxide carbon converted to carbon dioxide at 44/12

  dplyr::transmute(Vegetation = vegetation, Subcategory = subcategory, `Biomass consumption (t/ha)` = pm(mb_cf, mb_cf_se, 1),
                   `Combustion factor` = pm(cf, cf_sd, 2), `Emission factor row` = dplyr::coalesce(ef_row, "")) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(Vegetation = "Organic soil, boreal and temperate", Subcategory = c("Wildfire (undrained peat)", "Wildfire (drained peat)"),

zone_defaults <- tibble::tribble(~gez_abbrev, ~gez_name, ~row_2_4, ~mb_cf, ~mb_cf_se, ~cf, ~cf_sd, ~ef_row,
  "Ba", "Boreal coniferous forest", "Boreal forest, wildfire (general)", 52.8, 48.4, 0.40, 0.06, "Extra tropical forest",

                   `Biomass consumption (t/ha)` = pm(mb_cf, mb_cf_se, 1), `Combustion factor` = pm(cf, cf_sd, 2), `IPCC emission factor row` = ef_row,
                   `CO2 (g/kg)` = pm(co2, co2_sd, 0), `CH4 (g/kg)` = pm(ch4, ch4_sd, 1), `N2O (g/kg)` = pm(n2o, n2o_sd, 2))

                co2e_mt = co2_mt + (ch4_kt * 28 + n2o_kt * 265) / 1e3,
                u_zone = sqrt(u_term(mb_cf_se, mb_cf)^2 + u_term(co2_sd, co2)^2))

  dplyr::summarise(u = sqrt(sum((u * co2_mt)^2)) / sum(co2_mt)) |>

# Equation 2.27 by stratum, each fire at the Table 2.4 row of its zone, fire type and month, and Equation 2.8 of the Wetlands Supplement added on organic soil
boreal_zones <- c("Ba", "Bb", "BM"); temperate_zones <- c("TeDc", "TeDo", "TeM"); grassland_zones <- c("TeBSk", "TeBWk")
row_of <- function(zone, type, season) dplyr::case_when(
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Crown" ~ "Boreal forest, Crown fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Surface" ~ "Boreal forest, Surface fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones ~ "Boreal forest, Wildfire (general)",
  zone %in% temperate_zones ~ "Other temperate forests, Wildfire",
  zone %in% grassland_zones & season %in% c("April to May", "June") ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, All savanna grasslands (early dry season burns)",
  zone %in% grassland_zones ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, Grassland (mid or late dry season burns)",
  zone == "P" ~ "Other vegetation types, Tundra")

  dplyr::inner_join(rows_2_4[, c("row", "mb_cf", "ef_row")], by = "row") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table_2_5, by = "ef_row") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dm_mt = ha * mb_cf / 1e6, co2_mt = dm_mt * co2 / 1e3, ch4_kt = dm_mt * ch4, n2o_kt = dm_mt * n2o,

# Biomass consumption on a 2 km grid, the Table 2.4 row of each cell's ecological zone and land cover class, with organic soil from the soil raster
grid <- terra::rast(terra::ext(sf::st_bbox(gez)), resolution = 2000, crs = "EPSG:3978")
zone_r <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(gez), grid, field = "gez_abbrev")
zone_code <- terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$gez_abbrev[match(terra::values(zone_r)[, 1], terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$ID)]
cover_code <- terra::values(terra::project(land_cover, grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
soil_code <- terra::values(terra::project(soil, grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
category <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(zone_code) ~ NA_character_, cover_code %in% c(1:5, 8, 9) ~ "Forest", cover_code %in% 6:7 ~ "Shrubland",
                             cover_code %in% 10:11 ~ "Grassland", cover_code %in% c(12, 14) ~ "Cropland", cover_code == 16 & zone_code == "P" ~ "Tundra",
                             .default = "Other")
category <- dplyr::if_else(zone_code == "P" & category %in% c("Shrubland", "Grassland"), "Tundra", category)
fuel <- dplyr::case_when(category == "Forest" & zone_code %in% c(boreal_zones, "P") ~ 52.8, category == "Forest" ~ 19.8, category == "Shrubland" ~ 14.3,
                         category == "Grassland" ~ 4.1, category == "Tundra" ~ 10, .default = NA_real_)
as_layer <- function(x, levels) { r <- terra::rast(grid); terra::values(r) <- factor(x, levels = levels); r }
# The rows of Table 1 that overlap on each cell, the vegetation row of Table 2.4 and the organic soil row of the Wetlands Supplement, for their areas
row_labels <- c("Boreal forest, mineral soil", "Boreal forest, organic soil", "Temperate forest, mineral soil", "Temperate forest, organic soil",
                "Shrubland", "Grassland", "Tundra")
row_class <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(fuel) ~ NA_character_, fuel == 52.8 & soil_code == 1 ~ row_labels[2], fuel == 52.8 ~ row_labels[1],
                              fuel == 19.8 & soil_code == 1 ~ row_labels[4], fuel == 19.8 ~ row_labels[3], fuel == 14.3 ~ row_labels[5],
                              fuel == 4.1 ~ row_labels[6], fuel == 10 ~ row_labels[7])
row_area <- tibble::tibble(row_class) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(row_class)) |> dplyr::count(row_class) |> dplyr::mutate(mha = n * 400 / 1e6)
soil_r <- as_layer(dplyr::if_else(is.na(zone_code) | soil_code == 0, NA_character_, soil_labels[pmax(soil_code, 1)]), soil_labels)
fuel_area <- tibble::tibble(category, fuel, zone_code) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(zone_code)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mha = dplyr::n() * 400 / 1e6, .by = c(category, fuel)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(-mha)
organic_mha <- sum(!is.na(fuel) & soil_code == 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 400 / 1e6
```

```{r}
fetch("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx")

inside <- !is.na(zone_code)
# Codes of the 2026 fuel type raster as its map service labels them, grouped to the fuel of the FBP System
fbp_code <- terra::values(terra::project(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff"), grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
fbp_labels <- c("Conifer, C-1 to C-7", "Mixedwood, M-1 and M-2", "Deciduous, D-1 and D-2", "Grass, O-1", "Vegetated non-fuel", "Non-fuel")
fbp_group <- dplyr::case_when(!inside ~ NA_character_, fbp_code %in% 1:7 ~ fbp_labels[1], fbp_code %in% c(415, 625, 650, 675) ~ fbp_labels[2],
                              fbp_code %in% c(11, 13) ~ fbp_labels[3], fbp_code %in% c(31, 32) ~ fbp_labels[4], fbp_code == 105 ~ fbp_labels[5],
                              fbp_code == 101 ~ fbp_labels[6], .default = NA_character_)
fbp_r <- as_layer(fbp_group, fbp_labels)
fbp_area <- tibble::tibble(fbp_group) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(fbp_group)) |> dplyr::count(fbp_group) |> dplyr::mutate(mha = n * 400 / 1e6) |> dplyr::arrange(-mha)

# Classes 1 to 9 of the peatland map are bog and fen, open, treed and forested; 0 is not peat
peat_code <- terra::values(terra::project(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif"), grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
peat_labels <- c("Open bog and fen", "Treed bog and fen", "Forested bog and fen")
peat_group <- dplyr::case_when(!inside ~ NA_character_, peat_code %in% 1:3 ~ peat_labels[1], peat_code %in% 4:6 ~ peat_labels[2],
                               peat_code %in% 7:9 ~ peat_labels[3], .default = NA_character_)
cfs_peat_r <- as_layer(peat_group, peat_labels)
mha_of <- function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE) * 400 / 1e6
ipcc_organic_mha <- mha_of(inside & soil_code == 1); cfs_peat_mha <- mha_of(inside & peat_code %in% 1:9)
both_peat_mha <- mha_of(inside & soil_code == 1 & peat_code %in% 1:9)

nbac <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", sheet = "sumstats_admin_name", skip = 2) |>
  dplyr::transmute(year = as.integer(YEAR), ha = as.numeric(CANADA)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(year))
nbac_2023 <- nbac$ha[nbac$year == 2023]

# The 2023 fires on the national peatland map and in the national fuel types
points_2023 <- sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/nfdb/raw/NFDB_point_shp.zip"), "/NFDB_point_20260811.shp"),
                           query = 'SELECT YEAR, SIZE_HA FROM "NFDB_point_20260811" WHERE YEAR = 2023', quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_transform(3978)
points_2023$peat <- terra::extract(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/ClassPeatMap_2020_EPSG_3978.tif"), terra::vect(points_2023))[, 2]
points_2023$fbp <- terra::extract(terra::rast("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff"), terra::vect(points_2023))[, 2]
cfs_peat_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$peat %in% 1:9]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
conifer_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% 1:7]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
mixed_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% c(415, 625, 650, 675)]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)
deciduous_share_2023 <- 100 * sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA[points_2023$fbp %in% c(11, 13)]) / sum(points_2023$SIZE_HA)

fbp_mha <- function(label) fbp_area$mha[fbp_area$fbp_group == label]
tier2_table <- tibble::tribble(~Quantity, ~`Tier 1 global default`, ~`National dataset`,
  "Forest fuel classes on the 2 km grid", sprintf("Two IPCC biomass consumption rows, boreal forest %.0f Mha and temperate forest %.0f Mha", fuel_area$mha[fuel_area$category == "Forest" & fuel_area$fuel == 52.8], fuel_area$mha[fuel_area$category == "Forest" & fuel_area$fuel == 19.8]),
    sprintf("FBP fuel types, conifer %.0f Mha, mixedwood %.0f Mha, deciduous %.0f Mha, grass %.0f Mha", fbp_mha(fbp_labels[1]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[2]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[3]), fbp_mha(fbp_labels[4])),
  "Biomass consumption (t dry matter per ha)", "IPCC biomass consumption table, 52.8 ± 48.4 boreal and 19.8 ± 6.3 temperate", "CBM-CFS3 disturbance matrices on the pools of each stand, with a burn severity sub-model from 2026",
  "Organic soil (Mha)", sprintf("IPCC default raster, %.0f", ipcc_organic_mha), sprintf("Peatland map, %.0f, of which %.0f also organic in the default raster", cfs_peat_mha, both_peat_mha),
  "Area burned in 2023 (Mha)", sprintf("MODIS MCD64A1 other forest as FAO published it, %.1f", burn_2023$ha / 1e6), sprintf("National Burned Area Composite, %.1f; fire points, %.1f", nbac_2023 / 1e6, sum(strata_2023$ha) / 1e6),
  "Area burned in 2023 on organic soil (%)", sprintf("IPCC default raster, %.0f", organic_share_2023), sprintf("Peatland map, %.0f", cfs_peat_share_2023),
  "Area burned in 2023 by fuel (%)", sprintf("MCD12Q1 forest %.0f, woody savanna and savanna %.0f", forest_share_2023, savanna_share_2023), sprintf("FBP conifer %.0f, mixedwood %.0f, deciduous %.0f", conifer_share_2023, mixed_share_2023, deciduous_share_2023),
  "Emission factors (g per kg)", "IPCC emission factor table, 1,569 carbon dioxide, 4.7 methane, 0.26 nitrous oxide", "Inventory split of combusted carbon, 90 per cent carbon dioxide, 9 per cent carbon monoxide, 1 per cent methane",
  "Natural share", "None", sprintf("Fire points cause field, %.0f per cent natural in 2023; inventory rule, every wildfire", natural_share_2023))
```

```{r}
#| label: faostat-burned
#| output: false

# MODIS/Terra+Aqua Burned Area Monthly L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, MCD64A1 version 6.1, bands BurnDate and Uncertainty, 2001 to 2024, read through Google Earth Engine
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD64A1.061
# MODIS/Terra+Aqua Land Cover Type Yearly L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, MCD12Q1 version 6.1, band LC_Type1 (IGBP classes), 2001 to 2023, read through Google Earth Engine
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD12Q1.061
# FAO Global Administrative Unit Layers 2015, level 0, the country boundary FAO's note names, Earth Engine collection FAO/GAUL/2015/level0
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/FAO_GAUL_2015_level0
# The burned area of FAO's method rebuilt as its note describes it: burned pixels of MCD64A1 with uncertainty below 20 per cent, the IGBP class
# of the yearly MCD12Q1 map (the 2022 map for 2023 and the 2023 map for 2024, the latest FAO had, which the rebuild showed), counted within the GAUL boundary, with every pixel also keyed by the ecological zone group of its Table 2.4 row
# and by whether the IPCC default soil raster calls its soil organic, so that the zone rows and the peat term can be applied to FAO's own burned area
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv")) {
  zone_groups <- gez |>
    dplyr::mutate(group = dplyr::case_when(gez_abbrev %in% boreal_zones ~ 1L, gez_abbrev == "P" ~ 3L, .default = 2L)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(group) |>
    dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_simplify(dTolerance = 2000) |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_transform(4326)
  geojson <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  sf::st_write(zone_groups, geojson, quiet = TRUE)
  organic_cells <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(soil == 1, dissolve = TRUE))
  organic_cells <- sf::st_set_crs(sf::st_make_valid(organic_cells[organic_cells[[1]] == 1, 1]), 4326)
  organic_geojson <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  sf::st_write(organic_cells, organic_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
  py <- reticulate::import_main()
  py$GEOJSON <- geojson
  py$ORGANIC <- organic_geojson
  py$CSV <- "02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv"
  py$UNC_MAX <- 20L
  py$TILES <- "02.inputs/faostat/raw/mcd64a1-tiles"
  reticulate::py_run_string(r"(
import ee, json, csv, os, time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
ee.Initialize(project='manuscripts-personal')
# The country, the zone groups and the organic soil enter as painted masks on plain rectangles, because a country polygon used as the
# reduction region is clipped against every tile and never returned for Canada, where the same polygon painted as a mask takes seconds
gaul = ee.FeatureCollection('FAO/GAUL/2015/level0').filter(ee.Filter.eq('ADM0_NAME', 'Canada'))
canada_mask = ee.Image().byte().paint(gaul, 1)
zones = ee.FeatureCollection([ee.Feature(ee.Geometry(f['geometry'], 'EPSG:4326', False), {'group': f['properties']['group']}) for f in json.load(open(GEOJSON))['features']])
organic = ee.FeatureCollection([ee.Feature(ee.Geometry(f['geometry'], 'EPSG:4326', False)) for f in json.load(open(ORGANIC))['features']])
base = ee.Image().byte().paint(zones, 'group').unmask(0).multiply(100).add(ee.Image().byte().paint(organic, 1).unmask(0).multiply(1000))
# Counted in the MODIS sinusoidal grid, where every pixel has the same area, so a pixel count times that area is the burned area exactly
modis = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').first().select('LC_Type1').projection()
scale = 463.3127165275
pixel_ha = scale * scale / 1e4
def year_key(year):
    lc_year = 2022 if year == 2023 else min(year, 2023)
    monthly = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD64A1').filterDate(f'{year}-01-01', f'{year + 1}-01-01')
    burned = monthly.map(lambda i: i.select('BurnDate').gt(0).And(i.select('Uncertainty').lt(UNC_MAX))).max()
    cover = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').filterDate(f'{lc_year}-01-01', f'{lc_year + 1}-01-01').first().select('LC_Type1')
    return cover.add(base).updateMask(burned).updateMask(canada_mask).rename(f'y{year}')
stack = ee.Image.cat([year_key(year) for year in range(2001, 2025)])
# Canada's extent in 96 boxes of 7.5 by 5.4 degrees, each a direct call holding all 24 years, six calls at a time, each box cached as it lands
os.makedirs(TILES, exist_ok=True)
lons = [-141.5 + i * 7.5 for i in range(13)]
lats = [41 + j * 5.4 for j in range(9)]
boxes = [(f'b{i:02d}{j:02d}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([lons[i], lats[j], lons[i + 1], lats[j + 1]], 'EPSG:4326', False)) for i in range(12) for j in range(8)]
def run_box(name, box, depth=0):
    path = f'{TILES}/{name}.json'
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return name
    try:
        hist = stack.reduceRegion(reducer=ee.Reducer.frequencyHistogram(), geometry=box, crs=modis, scale=scale, maxPixels=1e11).getInfo()
    except Exception as e:
        if depth >= 2 or 'time' not in str(e).lower():
            raise
        c = box.coordinates().getInfo()[0]
        x0, y0 = c[0]; x1, y1 = c[2]; xm, ym = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2
        hist = {}
        for k, (p, q, r, s) in enumerate(((x0, y0, xm, ym), (xm, y0, x1, ym), (x0, ym, xm, y1), (xm, ym, x1, y1))):
            run_box(f'{name}_{k}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([p, q, r, s], 'EPSG:4326', False), depth + 1)
            for band, h in json.load(open(f'{TILES}/{name}_{k}.json')).items():
                for key, n in (h or {}).items():
                    hist.setdefault(band, {})
                    hist[band][key] = hist[band].get(key, 0) + n
    json.dump(hist, open(path, 'w'))
    return name
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
    for done in as_completed([pool.submit(run_box, name, box) for name, box in boxes]):
        done.result()
counts = {}
for name, _ in boxes:
    for band, h in json.load(open(f'{TILES}/{name}.json')).items():
        for key, n in (h or {}).items():
            counts[(int(band[1:]), int(float(key)))] = counts.get((int(band[1:]), int(float(key))), 0) + n
with open(CSV, 'w', newline='') as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['year', 'land_cover_year', 'organic', 'zone_group', 'igbp', 'ha'])
    w.writeheader()
    for (year, k), n in sorted(counts.items()):
        w.writerow({'year': year, 'land_cover_year': 2022 if year == 2023 else min(year, 2023), 'organic': k // 1000, 'zone_group': (k // 100) % 10, 'igbp': k % 100, 'ha': n * pixel_ha})
)")
}
mcd <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/mcd64a1-burned-by-stratum.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(2001:2024 %in% mcd$year))

# FAO's items from the IGBP classes, forest as classes 1 to 5, and its fuel as the Table 2.4 rows its recovered coefficients matched
item_of <- function(igbp) dplyr::case_when(igbp %in% 1:5 ~ "Other forest", igbp == 8 ~ "Woody savanna", igbp == 9 ~ "Savanna", igbp == 10 ~ "Grassland",
                                           igbp == 7 ~ "Open shrubland", igbp == 6 ~ "Closed shrubland")
rebuilt <- mcd |>
  dplyr::mutate(item = item_of(igbp)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dplyr::case_when(item == "Other forest" & zone_group == 2 ~ table_2_4$fuel[2], item == "Other forest" ~ table_2_4$fuel[1],
                                        item == "Woody savanna" ~ table_2_4$fuel[3], item %in% c("Savanna", "Grassland") ~ table_2_4$fuel[4],
                                        item == "Open shrubland" ~ table_2_4$fuel[5], item == "Closed shrubland" ~ table_2_4$fuel[6])) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), dm = sum(ha * fuel), .by = c(year, item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(co2_kt = dplyr::if_else(item == "Other forest", dm * table_2_5$co2[1] / 1e6, NA_real_),
                ch4_kt = dm * table_2_5$ch4[1] / 1e6, n2o_kt = dm * table_2_5$n2o[1] / 1e6)
published <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% unique(rebuilt$item)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Biomass burned (dry matter)" ~ "dm", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2_kt",
                                            "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4_kt", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o_kt")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(element)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(year, item), names_from = element, values_from = value)
check <- dplyr::inner_join(rebuilt, published, by = c("year", "item"), suffix = c("_rebuilt", "_fao"))
# How closely the rerun reproduced the published hectares, by year over the five items and by item and year, and the forest fuel it implies
repro_year <- dplyr::summarise(check, ratio = sum(ha_rebuilt) / sum(ha_fao), .by = year)
repro_item <- dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(check, ha_fao > 0), ratio = ha_rebuilt / ha_fao)
repro_within_2 <- 100 * mean(abs(repro_item$ratio - 1) <= 0.02)
forest_2023 <- dplyr::filter(mcd, year == 2023, igbp %in% 1:5)
fao_fuel_2023 <- sum(forest_2023$ha * dplyr::if_else(forest_2023$zone_group == 2, table_2_4$fuel[2], table_2_4$fuel[1])) / sum(forest_2023$ha)

# The guidelines' own Tier 1 on FAO's burned area: every burned pixel at the Table 2.4 row and the Table 2.5 row of its ecological zone group, as the zone
# rebuild applied them to the fire points, and the peat term of Equation 2.8 on the pixels the soil raster calls organic, with the built up, snow, barren,
# water and unclassified pixels left out as FAO's note excludes them
group_rows <- zone_defaults |>
  dplyr::filter(gez_abbrev %in% c("Ba", "TeDc", "P")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(zone_group = c(Ba = 1L, TeDc = 2L, P = 3L)[gez_abbrev]) |>
  dplyr::select(zone_group, row_2_4, mb_cf, co2, ch4, n2o)
tier1_fao_area <- mcd |>
  dplyr::filter(zone_group %in% 1:3, !igbp %in% c(0, 13, 15, 16, 17)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), organic_ha = sum(ha[organic == 1]), .by = c(year, zone_group)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(group_rows, by = "zone_group") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dm_mt = ha * mb_cf / 1e6, co2_mt = dm_mt * co2 / 1e3, ch4_kt = dm_mt * ch4, n2o_kt = dm_mt * n2o,
                co2e_mt = co2_mt + (ch4_kt * 28 + n2o_kt * 265) / 1e3,
                peat_mt = organic_ha * peat_fuel[["mean"]] / 1e6, peat_co2_mt = peat_mt * peat_ef$co2 / 1e3, peat_ch4_kt = peat_mt * peat_ef$ch4,
                peat_co2e_mt = peat_co2_mt + peat_ch4_kt * 28 / 1e3)
rung2_2023 <- dplyr::filter(tier1_fao_area, year == 2023) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), organic_ha = sum(organic_ha), co2_mt = sum(co2_mt), ch4_kt = sum(ch4_kt), n2o_kt = sum(n2o_kt), co2e_mt = sum(co2e_mt),
                   peat_co2_mt = sum(peat_co2_mt), peat_ch4_kt = sum(peat_ch4_kt), peat_co2e_mt = sum(peat_co2e_mt))

# The 2023 estimate rung by rung, each rung replacing one input of the rung above, carbon dioxide equivalent at the inventory's warming potentials
co2e_of <- function(co2_kt, ch4_kt, n2o_kt) (sum(co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) + 28 * sum(ch4_kt) + 265 * sum(n2o_kt)) / 1e3
fao_2023_items <- dplyr::filter(published, year == 2023)
rebuilt_2023 <- dplyr::filter(rebuilt, year == 2023)
ladder <- tibble::tribble(~Estimate, ~`Burned area`, ~`Fuel and emission factors`, ~ha, ~co2_mt, ~ch4_kt, ~co2e_mt,
  "FAO as published", "MCD64A1 by MCD12Q1 class", "One fuel value per item, savanna factors",
    sum(fao_2023_items$ha), sum(fao_2023_items$co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e3, sum(fao_2023_items$ch4_kt), co2e_of(fao_2023_items$co2_kt, fao_2023_items$ch4_kt, fao_2023_items$n2o_kt),
  "FAO rebuilt from its note", "MCD64A1 by MCD12Q1 class", "The same",
    sum(rebuilt_2023$ha), sum(rebuilt_2023$co2_kt, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e3, sum(rebuilt_2023$ch4_kt), co2e_of(rebuilt_2023$co2_kt, rebuilt_2023$ch4_kt, rebuilt_2023$n2o_kt),
  "Tier 1 by zone on FAO's area", "MCD64A1 by ecological zone", "IPCC rows of the zone",
    rung2_2023$ha, rung2_2023$co2_mt, rung2_2023$ch4_kt, rung2_2023$co2e_mt,
  "Tier 1 by zone and soil on FAO's area", "MCD64A1 by zone and soil class", "The same, with the peat term on organic soil",
    rung2_2023$ha, rung2_2023$co2_mt + rung2_2023$peat_co2_mt, rung2_2023$ch4_kt + rung2_2023$peat_ch4_kt, rung2_2023$co2e_mt + rung2_2023$peat_co2e_mt,
  "Tier 1 by zone on the fire points", "Fire points by ecological zone", "The same",
    sum(zone_2023$ha), sum(zone_2023$co2_mt), sum(zone_2023$ch4_kt), sum(zone_2023$co2e_mt),
  "Tier 1 by stratum with the peat term", "Fire points by zone, fire type and soil", "Rows by fire type and the Wetlands Supplement",
    sum(strata_2023$ha), sum(strata_2023$co2_mt + strata_2023$peat_co2_mt), sum(strata_2023$ch4_kt + strata_2023$peat_ch4_kt), veg_2023 + peat_2023)
ladder_table <- dplyr::transmute(ladder, Estimate, `Burned area`, `Fuel and emission factors`, `Burned (Mha)` = sprintf("%.1f", ha / 1e6),
                                 `CO2 (Mt)` = sprintf("%.0f", co2_mt), `CH4 (kt)` = sprintf("%.0f", ch4_kt), `CO2e (Mt)` = sprintf("%.0f", co2e_mt))
```
